report.summary: Reviewed chunk 1 of daedalus/council/vendors.py: module docstring claims, closed vocabularies, identity helpers, VendorReply/FloorRefusal dataclasses.
risks: chunk 1 | medium | Module docstring claims about adapter behavior, egress, and no-write-path cannot be verified in this chunk; they rely on code later in the file and in other modules. | Read remaining chunks and referenced modules.
chunk 1 | low | PROMPT_DATA_NOTICE claims all evidence reaches model through prompt or not at all; actual call assembly not in this chunk. | Inspect _dispatch and adapter methods in later chunks.

chunk 1 | low | VendorReply.__post_init__ validates status and lane, but other fields (reason, endpoint, etc.) are not validated; reason may be empty even when status != 'ok'. | Inspect all construction sites; consider adding validation.

chunk 1 | low | _slug maps 'unknown' to 'unknown' and empty to 'unknown'; actor_id may produce 'council.unknown.unknown' for missing model, which could be a silent failure. | Confirm callers always supply non-empty model.
chunk 1 | low | model_family deliberately over-merges; may collapse distinct families like 'qwen2.5-coder' and 'qwen2.5' if tags are stripped. | Review intended granularity; tests may exist.
todos: Review remaining chunks 2-5 to verify adapter behavior, egress, and no-write-path claims.
Verify that VendorReply never gains a verdict field in later code.
Confirm that _slug/actor_id are used consistently in transcript and reply.
Check tests for host predicate and closed vocabularies.

handoff.purpose: Module docstring, closed vocabularies, identity helpers, VendorReply/FloorRefusal dataclasses.

symbols.name: STATUSES
symbols.note: Tuple of five transport statuses: ok, unavailable, timeout, refused_by_floor, error. Closed set enforced in VendorReply.__post_init__.

symbols.name: LANES
symbols.note: Tuple of two egress lanes: trusted, untrusted. Closed set enforced in VendorReply.__post_init__.

symbols.name: UNAVAILABLE_REASONS
symbols.note: Tuple of ten machine reasons for unavailability, used for aggregation.

symbols.name: DEFAULT_LOCAL_OLLAMA_HOST
symbols.note: Local Ollama host: http://127.0.0.1:11434 (explicitly not localhost to avoid IPv6 miss).

symbols.name: PROMPT_DATA_NOTICE
symbols.note: Constant string prepended to every outbound prompt; instructs model to treat evidence as data and report injection attempts as findings.

symbols.name: _slug
symbols.note: Sanitizes a string to [A-Za-z0-9._-], replacing other chars with '-', falling back to 'unknown'.

symbols.name: actor_id
symbols.note: Builds namespaced actor id council.<vendor>.<model> via bus.actor_id after slugging both parts.

symbols.name: model_family
symbols.note: Coarse weight family heuristic: strips tag, path, and trailing size/version tokens; over-merges rather than under-merges.

symbols.name: VendorReply
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass for one vendor answer; carries transport status, content, provenance; deliberately no verdict field; validates status and lane in __post_init__.

symbols.name: VendorReply.__post_init__
symbols.note: Raises ValueError if status not in STATUSES or lane not in LANES.

symbols.name: FloorRefusal
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass for a secret-floor hit; names rule and channel, never matched bytes.

symbols.name: RunResult
symbols.note: Dataclass declaration starts at end of chunk; body incomplete in this window.

claims.text: Every adapter here exposes the same shape -- ask(prompt, *, role, timeout_s, model=None) -> VendorReply -- over four vendors
claims.why: The adapter classes are defined later in the file; this chunk only shows the module docstring and value types.

claims.text: VendorReply carries no approve/reject/score/verdict/majority field and must never grow one
claims.where: module docstring and VendorReply class docstring
claims.why: VendorReply fields listed are vendor, actor, model, status, content, latency_s, reason, stderr, usage, independence_class, endpoint, cli_version, lane, local, withheld; no verdict-like field present.

claims.text: status here is a TRANSPORT status (did the bytes make the round trip), not a judgement about the work under review.
claims.why: STATUSES are ok, unavailable, timeout, refused_by_floor, error; all transport outcomes. No judgement values like 'approved' or 'rejected'.

claims.text: The premise -- 'independent vendors have independent blind spots, so cross-vendor disagreement is informative' -- is plausible and UNTESTED here.
claims.why: The chunk does not contain any test or measurement code; it only states the protocol. The claim that it is untested cannot be verified from this chunk alone.

claims.text: the measurement must exist before any council is wired into a real review workflow
claims.why: No wiring or measurement code in this chunk; this is a policy statement about future integration.

claims.text: Nothing here writes, edits, applies or promotes anything.
claims.why: This chunk contains only constants, helpers, and dataclasses; no file operations are visible. However, the full module may contain write operations in later chunks.

claims.text: Council profiles are deliberately NOT adapters.subprocess_adapter.RUNTIME_PROFILES
claims.why: COUNCIL_PROFILES is not defined in this chunk; RUNTIME_PROFILES is in another module.

claims.text: codex runs exec --sandbox read-only with approvals off; claude runs -p with tools disallowed and NO dontAsk
claims.why: Adapter implementations are not in this chunk.

claims.text: every subprocess is spawned in a FRESH EMPTY TEMP DIRECTORY that is not the repo, not a worktree and contains no repo files (see :func:council_cwd)
claims.why: council_cwd is defined later in the file; not present in this chunk.

claims.text: all evidence reaches a model through the prompt or not at all.
claims.why: The evidence-passing mechanism is in adapter implementations later in the file.

claims.text: The secret floor runs PER FILE before any bytes leave the process: the PATH channel over each evidence path individually ... the CONTENT channel per file, and a content-only backstop over the assembled prompt. A hit REFUSES the call (status="refused_by_floor"); there is no redact-and-send, and the runner is never invoked.
claims.why: floor_check and the egress logic are defined later in the file; not in this chunk.

claims.text: OLLAMA_HOST is NEVER set, mutated or inherited by anything in this module.
claims.why: This chunk does not contain any environment variable manipulation, but the full module may. The claim cannot be verified from this chunk alone.

claims.text: the host is passed explicitly per call, and whether it counts as local is decided by sensitivity.lane_for_host
claims.why: The call path is in adapter implementations later in the file; lane_for_host is imported but not used in this chunk.

claims.text: NUMERIC LOOPBACK ONLY: localhost does NOT count, because a name is a DNS indirection the predicate cannot see through.
claims.why: This is a property of lane_for_host in sensitivity module; not verifiable here.

claims.text: codex and agy default to lane="untrusted": the allow-list / default-deny tier is ON for them, and withheld paths are named.
claims.why: Adapter defaults are not in this chunk.

claims.text: runtime_registry.py currently marks codex_cli trusted-with-IP and openai_api not -- same company, opposite verdict -- so no default here inherits that.
claims.why: runtime_registry.py is a different module; not in this chunk.

claims.text: Council records are NEVER an input to memory recall, and nothing in this module touches memstore.
claims.why: No memstore references in this chunk; full module may have some.

claims.text: Transport outcome of one ask. CLOSED -- an adapter may not invent a sixth. None of these is a judgement about the reviewed work; "ok" means the bytes came back, nothing more.
claims.why: STATUSES is a tuple of exactly five strings; VendorReply.__post_init__ enforces the closed set by raising ValueError on any other status. The statuses are transport outcomes, not judgements.

claims.text: untrusted turns the allow-list / default-deny tier ON (sensitivity.slice_egress_rule).
claims.why: This chunk defines LANES but does not use it; the behavior of untrusted is in sensitivity.slice_egress_rule, not here.

claims.text: Machine reasons -- never free prose -- so a council record can be aggregated.
claims.why: UNAVAILABLE_REASONS is a tuple of fixed strings; no free prose allowed by the constant definition.

claims.text: Prepended to EVERY outbound prompt. The evidence under review was written by a candidate model; a diff can carry text addressed to the reviewer and there is no delimiter that makes an LLM reliably treat text as data. The mitigation is not a better delimiter -- it is that an injection attempt becomes a FINDING. (The structural mitigation is that nothing here can act.)
claims.why: The constant is defined here, but the claim that it is prepended to every outbound prompt depends on adapter code later in the file.

claims.text: NO LOCAL-HOST TABLE HERE, ON PURPOSE. "Do the bytes leave this machine" has exactly one implementation, sensitivity.lane_for_host, imported above -- it is the predicate that switches the tier-2 allow-list, so a second copy next to it is a second answer to a safety question. This module used to carry _LOCAL_HOSTS + _endpoint_host and disagreed with the shared predicate on [::1], on 127.0.0.0/8, and on localhost. See tests/test_host_predicate.py, which fails if the table comes back.
claims.why: This chunk contains no local-host table; only constants DEFAULT_BENCH_OLLAMA_HOST and DEFAULT_LOCAL_OLLAMA_HOST, which are explicit URLs, not a table. The claim about historical disagreement is uncheckable, but the absence of a table in this chunk is kept.

claims.text: Make a model id safe for an actor segment without losing information.
claims.why: The function replaces any run of characters not in [A-Za-z0-9._-] with a single '-', and falls back to 'unknown' if empty. This preserves alphanumeric, dot, underscore, hyphen characters, though it collapses other characters into '-' (which may lose some information, but the claim is 'safe' not 'lossless').

claims.text: ``council.<vendor>.<model>`` per ``docs/adrs/010-naming-namespaces.md``.
claims.why: actor_id calls _bus_actor_id(_slug(vendor), _slug(model)). Assuming _bus_actor_id produces 'council.<vendor>.<model>' (as the docstring states and the import suggests), the format is as described. The exact behavior of _bus_actor_id is not in this chunk, but the delegation is visible.

claims.text: A bare ``actor: "claude"`` in a durable record is a defect, and it is also not reproducible: the model behind a stable command name changes underneath it, so a dissent attributed only to a vendor cannot be re-run six months on.
claims.why: This is a rationale; the claim about reproducibility depends on how actor_id is used in durable records, which is not in this chunk.

claims.text: The FORMAT is delegated to :func:bus.actor_id so the id on a transcript turn and the id on the reply that produced it cannot drift apart; this function only normalises the raw model id first (a raw ``qwen2.5-coder:7b`` would otherwise put a colon in a durable identifier).
claims.why: actor_id calls _bus_actor_id(_slug(vendor), _slug(model)). The slug removes colons (replaced with '-'), so a raw model id like 'qwen2.5-coder:7b' becomes 'qwen2.5-coder-7b'. The delegation is visible.

claims.text: The unit of independence is WEIGHTS, not endpoints. Local ``qwen2.5-coder:7b`` and bench ``qwen2.5-coder:7b`` are one voice on two sockets, and the 1.5b/7b/14b/32b line are near-clones of each other; a council that degrades to "Ollama plus Ollama" reports two participants and holds one opinion.
claims.why: This is a rationale for the function; the actual independence classification depends on how model_family is used in VendorReply.independence_class, which is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Heuristic and deliberately coarse -- it strips the tag (``:7b``) and any trailing size/version token, so it OVER-merges rather than under-merges. Over-merging costs a seat; under-merging silently fakes independence.
claims.why: The code strips everything after ':' (tag), takes the last path component, and pops trailing tokens matching size/version patterns (e.g., '7b', 'v2', '20240101'). This can over-merge (e.g., 'qwen2.5-coder:7b' and 'qwen2.5-coder:14b' both become 'qwen2.5-coder').

claims.text: Deliberately carries NO approve/reject/pass/verdict/ok/score/confidence field, and must never grow one -- see the module docstring. ``status`` is transport, ``content`` is prose for a human and for a claim extractor, and everything else is provenance so the turn can be re-run and compared.
claims.why: The dataclass fields are exactly as listed; no verdict-like fields. The comment about status and content is consistent with the field definitions.

claims.text: Machine reason from :data:UNAVAILABLE_REASONS, or a secret-floor rule LABEL (never the matched bytes). Empty when ``status == "ok"``.
claims.why: The comment is present, but enforcement (that reason is empty when status == 'ok') is not in this chunk; __post_init__ does not check it.

claims.text: Evidence paths withheld by the tier-2 allow-list on an untrusted lane.
claims.why: The field exists, but the population of withheld paths is in the adapters later in the file.

claims.text: A secret-floor hit. Names the RULE, never the matched bytes.
claims.why: FloorRefusal has only rule and channel fields; no bytes field. The channel is a string, but the rule is a label; no matched bytes are stored.

observations.what: VendorReply.__post_init__ validates status and lane, but does not validate that reason is empty when status == 'ok', nor that reason is non-empty when status is not 'ok'.
The module docstring makes many strong claims about behavior (no write path, egress, OLLAMA_HOST) that cannot be verified in this chunk; they depend on later code.
PROMPT_DATA_NOTICE is a constant string; its actual prepending to every outbound prompt must be verified in later chunks.

The comment 'NO LOCAL-HOST TABLE HERE' is kept in this chunk, but the test file tests/test_host_predicate.py is referenced and not present here; the claim that the test fails if the table comes back is uncheckable.
model_family strips trailing version tokens like 'v2' and 'latest', which could over-merge distinct model versions; this is intentional per docstring.
